ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) under the AML/CFT Act 2009, including screening of Directors, Shareholders, Ultimate Beneficial Owners and authorized signatories against the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2021, New Zealand consolidated sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC (Office of Foreign Assets Control, US Treasury) consolidated sanctions list, Her Majesty's Treasury (UK) financial sanctions list, and the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) listed jurisdictions. Screening must run continuously and be documented in an AML/CFT risk assessment and compliance programme per AML/CFT Act 2009 and the Financial Markets Authority regulations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Register of Companies (online portal: https://app.companiesoffice.govt.nz/companiesapp/pages/home.aspx)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English or Maori; names using characters other than the Latin alphabet (or without a standard romanised rendering) must be transliterated into the English / Latin alphabet for registration. Names must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, reserved name, or overseas company registered in New Zealand, and must comply with Companies Act 1993 s.22 and the associated Name Availability Guidelines published by the New Zealand Companies Office.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Tapui Limited' or other mandatory liability suffix depending on entity form (permitted use is required, not prohibited)

'Crown', 'Government', 'Ministry', 'National', 'Reserve Bank', 'Treasury', 'Inland Revenue', 'Authority', 'Commission', 'Bank', 'Insurance', 'Trust', 'Trustee', 'University', 'Institute', 'Incorporated', 'Chartered', 'Registered', 'Accredited', 'Certified', 'Exchange', 'Clearing House', 'Settlement', 'Market Making', 'High Frequency Trading', 'Algorithmic Trading', 'Financial Advice', 'Financial Adviser', 'Broker' (where prior ministerial or Financial Markets Authority approval / licence is required), 'Co-operative', 'Building Society', 'Specialist', 'Fund Manager', 'Hedge Fund' (without relevant licence or consent)
Any token implying Crown sponsorship or royal patronage
Any token containing 'AML' or 'CFT' where the entity will not be an AML/CFT reporting entity
Any token using 'NZ', 'New Zealand', or 'Aotearoa' without Companies Office consent
Any token that is offensive or contrary to public policy under the Companies Act 1993
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the New Zealand Companies Office within 10 working days from the date of rejection, submitting legal arguments and any supporting consents from relevant authorities (e.g., FMA, RBNZ, overseas regulator). If reconsideration fails, the applicant may file an appeal under s.22(4) of the Companies Act 1993 to the High Court of New Zealand, or apply to reserve a new name with a different proposed name. An administrative appeal may also be made under the Ombudsmen Act 1977 in respect of administrative action by a government agency, though the primary statutory appeal route is to the High Court. The name holder may file a fresh application after the rejection decision and may request an extension of existing reservation if the rejection is resolved within the 20-day validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is generally acceptable for registered office purposes under s.192 of the Companies Act 1993, provided there is a physical address in New Zealand at which legal documents may be served; however, for a regulated financial services entity engaged in algorithmic high-frequency trading / proprietary trading, the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and Inland Revenue Department (IRD) require genuine commercial substance, including a physical New Zealand business address or colocation / data-centre location if trading through a domestic exchange, and a local compliance and governance function. Virtual-office-only arrangements, where no real staff, infrastructure or decision-making occurs in New Zealand, are at high risk of being treated as a sham, creating AML/CFT non-compliance, tax residence concerns and exercise of the Commissioner's anti-avoidance powers under the Income Tax Act 2007.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Very Likely / High – For a financial services business (HFT/prop trading), there is a significant probability (estimated at greater than 80% within the first twelve months of operation) that the FMA or the Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment (MBIE) will conduct either an announced or unannounced physical inspection or business premises review, particularly if the registered office is a virtual office, or if trading revenue is generated via high-turnover activities in funds transfer or clearing operations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), particularly sections 10 (Incorporation), 15 (Application for Registration), 18 (Certificate of Incorporation), 19 (Company Constitution optional), 21-24 (Registered Office), 42-50 (Share Allotment and Capital), 122-126 (Board of Directors), 128-130 (Board Resolutions), and 151-152 (Directors' Duties); supplemented by the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) guidance for financial services providers and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 for any licensed financial activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment (MBIE), operating the Companies Register at https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz/.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZ1 - 'Application for Incorporation of a Company' (electronic submission via the New Zealand Companies Office online registration portal), together with a Company Constitution (if adopted) and written consents to act as directors and shareholders.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the Companies Act 1993; a company may be incorporated with zero share capital and shares may be issued for consideration determined by the board. No escrow account or capital deposit is mandated for a general International Company. However, if the company seeks licensing as a financial service provider or market maker under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, additional fit-and-proper capital requirements may apply at the discretion of the FMA.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [●] LIMITED (the 'Company') dated [●], 20[●]. RESOLVED THAT: (1) The registration of the Company under the Companies Act 1993 be and is hereby ratified and confirmed, and the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the New Zealand Companies Office be accepted and placed in the corporate records. (2) The registered office of the Company shall be situated at [●], New Zealand, and that address be recorded with the Companies Office as the registered office pursuant to section 21 of the Companies Act 1993. (3) The directors hereby adopt the Constitution of the Company as presented to this meeting, subject to any amendments registered with the Companies Office. (4) The issued share capital of the Company be and is hereby approved as set forth in the share register, and the allotment of [●] ordinary shares at [●] per share to the subscribers named in the application for incorporation be ratified, with consideration satisfied in accordance with section 47 of the Companies Act 1993. (5) The following persons be and are hereby appointed as directors of the Company for a term expiring at the close of the next annual meeting: [name], [name]; and any vacancies shall be filled in accordance with the Constitution. (6) [Name] be and is hereby appointed as Company Secretary and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, each to serve at the pleasure of the board. (7) The directors be and are hereby authorized to open and maintain bank and broker accounts, to execute client and counterparty agreements, and to retain legal, accounting, and compliance advisers in connection with the Company's proprietary algorithmic trading and market-making operations. (8) The directors be and are hereby authorized to take all steps necessary to register the Company with the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR), to obtain any industrial or environmental permits, and to file all statutory returns. This Resolution was passed unanimously by written consent pursuant to section 122 of the Companies Act 1993. /s/ Chairperson

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – Name Reservation portal (https://nzrs.companiesoffice.govt.nz/name-reservation/)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a search of the New Zealand Companies Register and File of Names to confirm the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing or reserved name, does not imply an association with the Crown or a government body, and does not contain restricted words (e.g., 'Bank', 'Trust', 'Fund Manager') unless approval is obtained from the relevant licensing authority. Submit a name reservation application electronically; pay the non-refundable fee on the portal; the reservation is granted for 20 working days, renewable for a further 20 working days. Review any objections lodged by the Registrar or third parties and promptly file a response with the Registrar's evaluation team if required.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in English
Name reservation application form
Payment of name reservation fee (NZD 27.80 approx.)
Special approval letter if using a restricted word (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of intention to refuse name registration, file a written submission within 5 working days; if refused, select an alternative name and resubmit. If a third party files a name objection, respond to the Companies Office's assessment; if the decision remains adverse, apply to the High Court for judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Incorporation Documents and Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company secretary or licensed incorporation agent for attestation, with electronic lodgement through the New Zealand Companies Office portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Constitution (optional but recommended) and complete Form NZ1 with details of the company name, registered office address, directors' full names, residential addresses and dates of birth, shareholder details, share structure, and address for service. Obtain signed consents to act as directors from each proposed director. Verify each director's identity using a certified copy of a passport or government-issued ID and, if applicable, obtain a New Zealand IRD number or declare an offshore address. Internal filing documents must be notarized if the company is incorporated by remote overseas shareholders; otherwise, digital signatures via the Companies Office system suffice.
required_dossiers: Form NZ1 - Application for Incorporation of a Company
Company Constitution (if adopting one)
Consent to act as director from each director
Certified identification documents (passport or national ID) for each director and shareholder
Address for service within New Zealand or in a jurisdiction permitted by the Registrar
Shareholder register and initial share allocation schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office queries any field (e.g., director's residential address non-disclosure), submit a Request for Name/Address Confidentiality via the portal or provide alternative service address. Correct any errors within the Registrar's specified deadline (normally 5 working days); if rejected, re-file the application and pay a fresh fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Office online portal using the RealMe authenticated account and submit the complete incorporation pack. The system performs immediate automated validation of company name, director eligibility (including disqualification checks), and shareholder information. Pay the prescribed registration fee of NZD 123.50 via the portal. Upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation with a unique company number (NZBN) and file registration date. The company must obtain an NZ Business Number (NZBN) automatically assigned at registration, and also register for tax (obtain an IRD number) through the same session or separately online via the Inland Revenue Department.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Form NZ1 incorporating any annexed constitution
Directors' consents to act
Payment confirmation
RealMe identity verification and IRD registration details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is automatically rejected due to data mismatch, correct the underlying fields and resubmit. If the Registrar later cancels registration under section 336 of the Companies Act 1993 for non-compliance, apply for restoration under section 337 within 2 years, or seek a court order under section 338.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution and Appointment of Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board of directors acting in the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a board meeting or execute a written resolution signed by all directors pursuant to section 122 of the Companies Act 1993. The first board resolution must ratify incorporation, adopt (or decline) the constitution, allot shares, approve the initial share register, fix the registered office, appoint the company secretary (if any), and authorize the opening of bank and trading accounts and engagement of a compliance officer. Minutes and resolution records must be signed and kept in the company's records at the registered office, and the board must document any conflict-of-interest declarations under section 140.
required_dossiers: Written board resolution or minutes of first board meeting
Share allotment records
Share certificates (if issued)
Registered office acceptance from the registered office provider or landlord
Appointment letters for company secretary and compliance officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any appointment is later invalidated for lack of consent, ratify by a subsequent board resolution and file a register refresh within 5 working days. If the Registrar requires an individual to act as a director, ensure that no person is disqualified and, if challenged, substitute a qualified director and file Form NZ2 (Change of Director Details) immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Register Refresh, Statutory Book Setup, and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company secretary / incorporation agent; Inland Revenue Department (IRD); Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 10 working days after incorporation, file the initial company register (shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners) if required under the financial reporting framework, and ensure the Companies Office online record is complete. Apply to the Inland Revenue Department for an IRD number (GST, income tax, and provisional tax), and elect a balance date. If conducting proprietary trading or market making with counterparties in New Zealand or from New Zealand, register on the Financial Service Providers Register unless an exemption applies. Implement corporate books and records including a share register, minute book, directors' interest register, and registers of charges and ultimate beneficial ownership. Establish a New Zealand bank account and, if needed, an overseas trading account with a clearing broker.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Artificial/natural person IRD registration form (IRD 394 or online)
Financial Service Providers Register application (if not exempt)
AML/CFT compliance programme summary (if applicable)
Proof of registered office and address for service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD delays issuing an IRD number due to outstanding corporate information, provide certified copies of the Certificate of Incorporation and director identity documents, and escalate in writing to the IRD. If the FSPR application is queried regarding fitness and propriety, respond within 10 working days with a written explanation and supporting evidence of qualifications or experience.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: New Zealand Financial Markets Authority (FMA) in conjunction with the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008; for physical trading-floor operations, the local council (territorial authority) under the Building Act 2004 and the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 enforced by WorkSafe New Zealand.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Financial Service Provider Registration (FSPR) – Category 'Derivatives Issuer' or 'Banks/Non-Bank Deposit Takers/Trustee Services' if applicable; alternatively a 'Market Making Licence' issued by an approved market operator (e.g., NZX or an ATS) and, where providing financial services to retail clients, a 'Financial Advice Provider' licence or 'Managed Investment Scheme' registration. For proprietary trading that does not interact with retail clients, the mandatory licence is the Financial Service Provider Registration authorizing the conduct of regulated financial services as a 'market maker' or 'other financial service provider'.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand (for nationally significant proposals) together with the relevant regional council under the Resource Management Act 1991 (RMA); for local data centers or trading server hosting facilities, the local territorial authority and regional council under an existing resource consent.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Limited/Exempt – Registration (Activity No. 9 of the RMA schedule); proprietary algorithmic trading infrastructure involving only server racks, HVAC systems, and backup generators typically does not trigger a full EIA report unless the facility exceeds thresholds for energy generation, hazardous substances storage, or discharges to air, water, or land. If a proposed trading server farm is hosted in an existing data center with an existing resource consent, no separate EIA is required; a standalone facility generally requires a 'Land Use Resource Consent' under the RMA and possibly an AEE (Assessment of Environmental Effects) if the activity is not a Permitted Activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Under the Resource Management Act 1991 and regional air plans, any discharges to air must comply with the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality (2004, amended 2019) – including a PM10 limit not to exceed 24-hour average of 50 µg/m³ and NOx emission limits for large combustion sources. Wastewater discharges from cooling or battery systems must meet the Regional Water Plan permissive standards (BOD < 20 g/m³; suspended solids < 40 g/m³; pH 6.0–8.5; temperature delta < 3°C above receiving-water ambient). Electronic waste (E-waste) from decommissioned servers must be managed under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and disposed of through an approved recycler; no ozone-depleting substances may be emitted from HVAC systems, and fluorinated greenhouse gases in refrigeration are regulated under the Ozone Layer Protection Act 1996.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) Act 2017 – an approved Evacuation Scheme and appropriate means of egress; a Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) issued by an Independent Qualified Person (IQP) under the Building Act 2004 for buildings containing a specified system (e.g., automated fire suppression, backup generator, computer room air conditioning); structural load compliance review for raised access floors and server rack concentrations; electrical certification and annual verification under the Electricity Act 1992; and a workplace health and safety assessment under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 demonstrating identification of hazards (thermal, electrical, psychological and ergonomic risks), a documented risk register, and welfare facilities. WorkSafe New Zealand clearance may be required if the facility undertakes energised electrical work or other prescribed high-risk activity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake), New Zealand Government — online services portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz). Goods export control and customs documentation are administered by the New Zealand Customs Service (Te Mana Ārai o Aotearoa) via the Trade Single Window (TSW).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident Cook Islands International Company must apply for an Inland Revenue (IRD) number before it derives New Zealand-source income, registers for GST, or becomes an employer. Procedure: (1) Prepare form IR742 — 'Non-Resident Company IRD Number Application' — attaching certified copies of the Cook Islands certificate of incorporation, constitution, current certificate of good standing, directors'/shareholders' identification, and proof of the New Zealand agent registration (if any). (2) Submit the application electronically through the 'Apply for an IRD number for an overseas company' service in myIR, or by post to Inland Revenue, PO Box 39010, Wellington 5045, New Zealand. (3) Await issuance of the 8- or 9-digit IRD number (typically within 8–10 working days). (4) Once the IRD number is issued, register for GST via myIR if the 12-month rolling value of taxable supplies made in New Zealand will exceed NZD 60,000, or voluntarily if below the threshold. (5) Appoint a New Zealand tax agent or authorised representative if no physical place of business is maintained, and file all returns (income tax, GST, NRWT, and employer obligations) under the non-resident tax profile.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — the CK_IC is treated in New Zealand as a non-resident foreign company subject to entity-level income tax only on New Zealand-sourced income (Income Tax Act 2007, ss BD 1, YD 4). It is not a pass-through vehicle, and its Cook Islands tax-exempt status (Tax_Exempt_Zone) does not confer any exemption in New Zealand.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in New Zealand. Available statutory elections include: (a) GST accounting basis election (invoice, payments, or hybrid) and GST filing frequency election (monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; (b) GST group election (s 55) for companies with common ownership to file consolidated GST returns; (c) approved issuer levy election (2% levy in substitution for non-resident withholding tax on related-party interest); and (d) balance date election (s 38 Income Tax Act 2007) with IRD approval. Hybrid and branch mismatch countermeasures (Part FM and Subpart FE Income Tax Act 2007) apply automatically and are not subject to elective opt-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a value-added/consumption tax imposed under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (GSTA 1985) and administered by Inland Revenue.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in New Zealand in any rolling 12-month period (s 51 GSTA 1985). This threshold applies equally to non-resident suppliers of remote/digital services and distance sellers of low-value goods (s 54B). Voluntary registration is available below the threshold, subject to the usual conditions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based continuous transaction control, or digital stamping regime is in force. E-invoicing is implemented on the PEPPOL network: businesses with New Zealand annual turnover above NZD 250 million (from 1 April 2022), NZD 50 million (from 1 April 2024), and NZD 10 million (from 1 April 2026) must be able to receive PEPPOL e-invoices. Inland Revenue provides a free PEPPOL e-invoicing service; the issuer chooses the PEPPOL access point. Tax invoices may be issued in paper or electronic form, and e-invoicing does not require prior authorisation or clearance by Inland Revenue.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available where: (1) goods are exported by the supplier from New Zealand within 28 days of supply (s 11(1)(a) GSTA 1985); (2) services are supplied to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, provided the services are not directly in connection with land or goods situated in New Zealand and the recipient is not in New Zealand when the services are performed (s 11(1)(m)); and (3) remote services are supplied to a non-resident business customer outside New Zealand under s 11(1)(mb) and schedule 3A. Caution: the CK_IC's proprietary ultra-low-latency algorithmic market-making, clearing, and exchange-related services are financial services (s 3 GSTA 1985) and are generally exempt (not zero-rated) under s 14 GSTA 1985; an exemption without input credit arises unless the services fall within an export zero-rating limb or the de minimis rules apply. Refund substantiation requires clearly attributable export documentation and, for exempt financial services, the denial of input credit must be considered.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Export Declaration (EX) lodged through the Trade Single Window, with the Customs clearance receipt
Bill of Lading (or Airway Bill / sea waybill) evidencing physical export from New Zealand within the statutory 28-day window
Inward foreign currency remittance evidence (bank SWIFT MT103 confirmation or broker settlement statement) evidencing payment for the exported goods or services
Executed service agreement, trade tickets, clearing/settlement records, and time-stamped order audit trail for zero-rated exported algorithmic trading services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: New Zealand does not prescribe a statutory FX repatriation deadline for GST zero-rating; the 180-day benchmark is used as an evidentiary expectation in IRD audits, with longer deferral requiring commercial justification. If the stated export conditions are not satisfied, the supply is taxable at 15% GST, and the supplier must account for the tax shortfall plus use-of-money interest. Penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% shortfall penalty for lack of reasonable care; 40% for taking an unacceptable tax position; up to 100% for evasion or fraudulent intent; voluntary disclosure may reduce penalties. The time bar for reassessment is 4 years, and it does not apply where returns are fraudulent or grossly carelessly filed. GST anti-avoidance provisions (s 76 GSTA 1985) allow recharacterisation of arrangements with the principal purpose of obtaining a tax advantage, and the general anti-avoidance rule (s GA 1 Income Tax Act 2007) applies. False export declarations to the New Zealand Customs Service attract separate civil penalties and criminal fines under the Customs and Excise Act 2018; IRD and NZ Customs jointly audit export inconsistencies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand - Te Pūtea Matua (RBNZ), acting as the monetary authority for the New Zealand dollar and operator of the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS); the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission is the domestic non-bank financial regulator for the International Company vehicle, with the Ministry of Finance and Economic Management overseeing any Cook Islands dollar note issuance at a fixed 1:1 parity to the NZD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar is fully and freely convertible on both the current account and the capital account. There are no New Zealand exchange control statutes imposing general convertibility restrictions for trade-related remittances, dividend distributions, loan repayments, or capital injections. Profit remittance from New Zealand to non-resident shareholders is not subject to FX licensing or central bank approval; it is subject solely to standard AML/CFT documentation and, where applicable, New Zealand non-resident withholding tax under the Income Tax Act 2007. For a Cook Islands International Company, foreign currency accounts can be maintained in New Zealand and Cook Islands licensed banks without prior RBNZ exchange control approval because no such surrender or conversion regime exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender obligation in New Zealand and no mandatory conversion ratio into NZD. Exporters, including a proprietary algorithmic trading entity earning offshore transaction revenues, may repatriate or retain export proceeds in the currency of settlement. New Zealand banks are required to report cross-border transactions and balance-of-payments statistical data to the RBNZ under the International Transactions Reporting regime, and all international wire transfers are subject to AML/CFT information requirements under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. The Cook Islands International Company has no separate surrender obligation; the NZD is the domestic currency and the entity is not subject to any exchange control surrender timeline.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. New Zealand does not operate a standalone EMI licence; offshore fintech/digital EMIs are permissible only as supplementary payment service providers, not as primary clearing banks. To be commercially viable, the offshore EMI must be registered on the New Zealand Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR), appoint a New Zealand-resident AML/CFT compliance officer, belong to an approved dispute resolution scheme, and route NZD settlements through a licensed New Zealand bank's clearing account. An unregistered offshore digital EMI cannot access ESAS and cannot provide a legally recognised New Zealand bank account for the International Company.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the AML/CFT Act, a New Zealand bank may rely on electronic identity verification, but the bank's own risk policy will ordinarily govern. In practice, for an offshore Cook Islands International Company, at least one director or an authorised senior officer will be required to attend an interview in person at a New Zealand branch or, alternatively, to appear before a New Zealand-recognised notary, lawyer, or embassy official for identity attestation. Remote onboarding is increasingly possible for low-risk and mid-tier accounts but is not guaranteed; a physical or notarised KYC meeting is effectively mandatory for foreign-registered companies, especially when the beneficial owners are non-resident.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt offshore International Company status without visible commercial substance triggers enhanced due diligence and negative media screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation; Certificate of Good Standing from the Cook Islands International Companies Registry; registered agent confirmation letter; constitutional documents; register of directors and shareholders; ultimate beneficial ownership declaration; a written commercial substance explanation confirming the algorithmic trading activity, trading premises or service provider arrangements, and a New Zealand IRD registration where activity is deemed to have a New Zealand nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and multi-jurisdictional beneficial owners create jurisdictional AML ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised or apostilled passport copies for all directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners; a certified corporate organisation chart; proof of residential address; bank and brokerage statements spanning at least six months; source of wealth memorandum; source of funds evidence for the initial capital contribution; and a legal opinion from a New Zealand or Cook Islands counsel confirming due incorporation and standing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Algorithmic high-frequency trading generates high transaction velocity, unusual counterparty geography, and substantial daily turnover, which may be misclassified as high risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or unaudited financial statements; detailed algorithm risk management and governance policy; trade execution and clearing venue licences; realistic monthly volume and liquidity projections; ISDA or prime brokerage agreements; SWIFT correspondence history with regulated counterparties; the entity's financial services registration status under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Disputes Resolution) Act 2008; and a definitive explanation that no retail-customer payment services are provided.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection from an overseas parent or third-party investor may raise source-of-funds concerns, particularly where funds arrive from a tax-exempt jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving the capital injection; subscription or shareholders' agreement; capital account ledger; remittance purpose statement; the actual SWIFT payment advice with a clear purpose code; investor's identity and tax residence documentation; bank or brokerage statements demonstrating the legal origin of funds; and, where applicable, a certificate from the Cook Islands International Companies registrar confirming no bearer shares are outstanding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The phrase 'high-frequency trading' and 'proprietary market making' in the application may be interpreted by KYC units as speculative or gaming-adjacent activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Use of precise legal nomenclature restricted to 'regulated proprietary algorithmic market making in exchange-traded or FX-eligible instruments'; a copy of the FMA or overseas market participant licence or exchange membership; a trading venue authorisation letter; confirmation that all trading is for the company's own account and that no third-party monies are held; and an undertaking to provide periodic transaction summaries upon request.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection must be routed as a SWIFT MT103 credit to the International Company's designated New Zealand bank account, with the beneficiary account presented in the New Zealand account number format (two-digit bank code, four-digit branch, seven-digit base account, and suffix). The remittance field must state the true purpose, for example 'equity capital contribution to International Company for proprietary trading operations', together with the receiving bank's prescribed inward remittance purpose or foreign investment code for direct investment into New Zealand. No prior RBNZ exchange control approval is required because New Zealand has no exchange control consent regime; however, the bank will perform AML/CFT verification and, for deposits and cross-border transactions above reporting thresholds, will automatically submit international transaction reporting to the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit. If the capital injection involves the acquisition of New Zealand sensitive land or significant business assets, the Overseas Investment Act 2005 consent requirements must be separately assessed, but ordinary Treasury and trading capital is exempt.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements and market-making settlements should be executed via regulated clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 for direct commercial wire payment, MT202 COV for correspondent bank cover payments, and commercial letters of credit issued under ICC UCP600 for goods-backed trade flows where relevant. NZD settlement must be effected through the RBNZ Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) via the settlement bank. US dollar legs of the proprietary trading activity will be cleared through Fedwire or CHIPS through the bank's correspondent network. For foreign-exchange market making requiring payment-versus-payment (PvP) risk mitigation, CLS settlement should be used for eligible currencies. For securities related to algorithmic market making, delivery-versus-payment (DvP) settlement through the applicable central securities depository is the mandatory rail. The treasury blueprint should maintain segregated funding between the New Zealand operational account, the Cook Islands International Company capital account, and any US clearing account to preserve clean audit trails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX spot and outright forwards in NZD and major convertible currencies, executed under ISDA 1992 or 2002 and a New Zealand governing law master agreement.
FX swaps (forex swaps) used for rolling and short-term liquidity transformation, subject to Board-approved counterparty credit limits.
Cross-currency swaps for long-term structural hedging among NZD, USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, and AUD.
Vanilla FX options purchased for downside protection or sold only when covered by an offsetting option position or an established market making inventory.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) permitted solely for residual emerging-market exposures where the underlying currency is non-convertible or illiquid; the NZD leg remains a standard deliverable component and all NDF contracts must be governed by ISDA master documentation.
Exchange-traded FX futures and options on regulated execution facilities, subject to the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 and applicable exchange membership rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act 1993, s. 208; Companies Regulations 1994, reg. 5)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 30 calendar days after the anniversary date of incorporation; the Registrar issues a reminder notice approximately one month before the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal default notice issued; failure to file within 20 working days of the notice triggers a late filing penalty of NZD 500 (approximately USD 310) and may lead to prosecution. Continued default gives the Registrar power to strike the company off the New Zealand register under Companies Act 1993, s. 318, with all assets vesting in the Crown.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (if FMC reporting entity or 'large' company under Companies Act 1993, s. 45; otherwise exemption certification may apply)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies) and Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for FMC reporting entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: FMC reporting entities: signed and filed with the Registrar within 20 working days of the date they are reported to shareholders and no later than 5 months after the balance date. Non-reporting large companies: filed within 20 working days of the date financial statements are signed and dated.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file financial statements is an offence under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 and Companies Act 1993; maximum penalties are NZD 100,000 for the company and NZD 25,000 per director for continuing offences, with possible civil liability and strike-off upon persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT Annual Compliance Report and Biennial Independent Audit (for licensed financial service providers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) as AML/CFT supervisor for the licensed proprietary trading entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual Compliance Report due within 4 months of the entity's balance date; Independent AML/CFT audit required at least once every 2 years under sections 59 and 60 of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Supervisor may order remedial action, impose a civil penalty of up to NZD 200,000 for a body corporate, suspend or cancel the financial service provider licence, and refer for criminal prosecution under the AML/CFT Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Director and Shareholder Register Audit Confirmation (Annual internal statutory registers review and update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Office / Company Directors; verified by the Registrar as part of the Annual Return filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at the date of the Annual Return; any director or shareholder change occurring during the year must be filed with the Companies Office within 10 working days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain statutory registers or to notify changes is an offence under Companies Act 1993, s. 188; the company and every director commit a default and are liable to a fine not exceeding NZD 10,000, plus potential strike-off for persistent non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies where (a) the company is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; (b) the company is 'large' under Companies Act 1993, s. 45 — i.e., total assets exceed NZD 60 million, total revenue exceeds NZD 30 million, or 50 or more full-time equivalent employees; or (c) shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights validly demand an audit. An exempt International Company may avoid audit only if it is not large, not an FMC reporting entity, and all shareholders have passed a unanimous exemption resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS) for FMC reporting entities and large companies; Simplified New Zealand GAAP (Small and Medium-Sized Entities regime) for eligible small and medium companies, as prescribed by the External Reporting Board (XRB).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand law does not require a standalone UBO annual filing. The Annual Return to the Companies Office must confirm the company's registered office, directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial ownership details as recorded on the share register. Any share transfer or change of beneficial control exceeding 25% must be recorded in the company's own beneficial ownership register, and for a licensed financial service provider must be reflected in the FMA AML/CFT Annual Compliance Report.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (general meetings and board meetings)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand levies a flat 28% corporate rate with no general tax holiday or zone-based exemption for New Zealand tax residents. Effective reliefs include the refundable Research and Development Tax Incentive (15% of eligible R&D expenditure), the Foreign Dividend Exemption for qualifying foreign shareholdings, the Approved Issuer Levy (2% on qualifying cross-border interest) as a substitute for NRWT, and the imputation credit system eliminating economic double taxation on distributed New Zealand-source profits. An International Company (IC) incorporated in a tax-exempt jurisdiction is not taxed domestically by that jurisdiction on offshore income; however, any IC whose central management and control is exercised in New Zealand is deemed a New Zealand tax resident (Income Tax Act 2007, s YB 4) and becomes taxable on worldwide income at 28%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory time limit (unlimited carry-forward), subject to satisfaction of the 49% shareholder continuity rule under s IA 5 of the Income Tax Act 2007; the business continuity test was abolished in 2014.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR4 (Company Income Tax Return), filed electronically via myIR (Inland Revenue secure online portal) or through IRD-endorsed tax accounting software and registered intermediaries.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with three provisional tax instalments during the income year for most companies)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return is due by 7 July of the following income year. A tax agent extension commonly moves the filing and terminal tax due date to 31 March of the year following the balance date. Non-standard balance dates require prior IRD approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique eight to nine digit tax file number allocated by Inland Revenue for the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An IC that becomes New Zealand tax resident must first apply for an IRD number via form IR742 before a return can be lodged.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: End date of the income year (fiscal period) covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: New Zealand's standard balance date is 31 March; an offshore IC should request IRD approval for a non-standard balance date where the algorithmic trading accounting period differs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from proprietary ultra-low-latency algorithmic market-making, high-frequency trading, and ancillary financial services before deduction of expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only New Zealand-sourced income and income attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment; genuinely offshore HFT income derived by a non-resident IC is outside the New Zealand tax net.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross interest income, prime-brokerage credit balances, securities-lending fees, and financing/repo income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude interest already subject to Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) or the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL); IRD withholding certificates must be retained and attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross dividends received from equity and index holdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Foreign Dividend Exemption may apply to a NZ-resident IC holding a substantial foreign shareholding; imputation credits received on New Zealand dividends must be recorded and reconciled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessable income after applying New Zealand tax adjustments, reconciled from the accounting net profit via the Schedule 15 reconciliation statement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile IFRS accounting profit to taxable income; treaty deductions and transfer-pricing adjustments are allowable only where arm's-length documentation has been prepared and retained.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 per month or part-month (capped at NZ$1,000 per return) under s 139A of the Tax Administration Act 1994; late payment penalties of 1% of the unpaid tax immediately, 4% after 7 days, and 1% per month subsequently; compound use-of-money interest accrues daily on unpaid tax at the IRD underpayment rate. Incorrect returns additionally attract shortfall penalties of 20% (unacceptable tax position) or 100% (abusive tax position).
